beats.spoken: Your website chat answers with AI. Do your customers know?

data.question: Do customers know an AI is answering?

beats.spoken: Since the second of August 2026, the transparency rules of the EU AI Act apply. They don't only cover big companies, but also businesses that use AI in a professional capacity.

For the chat, the rule is: people must be told that they're talking to an AI. The duty lies with the provider. If you built the chat yourself and run it under your own name, then according to the European Commission, that's you.
The notice must be clear and distinguishable, at the latest at the first interaction. The only exception is when it's obvious to a reasonably attentive person that they're talking to an AI.

Second rule: deepfakes. If you publish AI images or videos at work that resemble real people or places and appear authentic, you must label them. Clearly drawn or impossible scenes usually don't count, according to the guidelines.
For your business, that means: say right away in the chat that an AI is answering. Label realistic AI images. And when uploading, set the AI label that TikTok, Instagram and YouTube offer.
